data.name: Mahibah
data.gender_notes: Mahibah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'h-b-h', meaning 'to love'. In Islam, Mahibah represents the essence of compassion, kindness, and deep affection towards others and Allah. The name Mahibah carries the meaning “Loving, Tender, Affectionate” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Mahibah usually hope their child will grow to embody loving, tender, affectionate and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of Allah's infinite love and mercy towards His creation.
data.etymology: Mahibah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Loving, Tender, Affectionate.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mahibah total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

It reflects the emphasis on love, kindness, and compassion towards all beings as taught in Islamic teachings. Mahibah is seen as an Arabic name that embodies the values of a good Muslim, one who is not only kind and compassionate towards fellow human beings but also towards all creatures and the environment.
data.spiritual_significance: Mahibah represents the spiritual depth of the meaning of compassion and love in Islam. This name signifies the divine love that Muslims are encouraged to nurture towards Allah and His creations. Mahibah is a reflection of God's infinite mercy and love towards His creation, and Muslims emulating these qualities are rewarded in the hereafter. The spiritual significance of the name Mahibah reminds Muslims to strive to attain a higher level of love and compassion for others and for the Creator, evoking the teachings of kindness and mercy as given in Islamic scripture and teachings.
